item.title: Biases in gaps between zeros of Dirichlet L-functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.31744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe a new family of Dirichlet L-functions that provably have an unusual value distribution. Experimentally, we find that the L-functions in this family have a significant and previously undetected bias in the distribution of gaps between their zeros. These phenomena appear to have an arithmetic explanation that corresponds to the nonvanishing of a certain Gauss-type sum. We give a complete classification of the characters for which this sum is nonzero and count them. This sum vanishes for 100% of primitive Dirichlet characters, so L-functions in our newly discovered family are rare (a set of density zero among all primitive characters). The nonvanishing of this sum implies that there is a main term when one integrates the Z-function associated to a Dirichlet L-function over a long interval. We prove that the L-functions in this family are the only GL(1)/Q or GL(2)/Q cuspidal automorphic L-functions whose Z-functions have a "large" mean value when integrated. We discuss analogous results for the Riemann zeta-function.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan W. Bober, Zhenchao Ge, Micah B. Milinovich

item.title: Divisor Sums with Spacing Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.31832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $x,y>0$ let $S(x,y)$ denote the largest value of $\sum_{n\in A}\tau(n)$ over subsets $A$ of $[1,x]\cap\N$ whose elements are pairwise separated by more than $y$ (here $\tau$ is the divisor function). We determine the order of magnitude, and in a subrange the precise asymptotic, of $S(x,y)$ when the spacing parameter $y$ ranges over a polylogarithmic scale $y=(\log x)^{1+\lambda(\log\lambda-1)}$, $\lambda>1$. We show that for every fixed $\lambda>2$ the spacing constraint costs a computable power of $\log x$ in the exponent, while for every fixed $1<\lambda<2$ it costs nothing at all: $S(x,y)\sim x\log x$, the same asymptotic as the unconstrained sum $\sum_{n\le x}\tau(n)$. Near the threshold $\lambda=2$ the two regimes meet, and we show that for any fixed $\kappa>0,$ $S(x,y)\asymp_{\kappa} x\log x$ uniformly as long as $\lambda\le 2+2\kappa/\sqrt{\log\log x}$. The proof combines the Sathe-Selberg distribution of the number of prime factors, a smooth squarefree estimate obtained from a generating function together with Cauchy's formula, a sieve estimate for correlations among the squarefree parts of the integers that contribute most heavily to $\sum_{n\le x}\tau(n)$, and two combinatorial devices (the Caro-Wei bound and a concentration inequality on the symmetric group) used to extract a well-spaced independent set from a sparse auxiliary graph.
item.dc:creator: Aahan Chatterjee

item.title: Quantitative nodal domain count for Maass forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.31857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a real even Hecke-Maass cusp form $\phi$ on the modular surface, with Laplace eigenvalue $1/4+T^2$. We prove that its restriction to any fixed compact segment $\beta$ of the vertical geodesic above $i$ has $\gg_{\beta,\varepsilon} T^{1/6-\varepsilon}$ sign changes, yielding the same lower bound for the number of distinct inert nodal domains meeting the segment. Building on ideas of Jang-Jung and Jung-Young, we study correlations between values at points on the vertical geodesic separated by distances of order $T^{-1}$. Using arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity and Dirichlet-polynomial estimates, we show that the correlation is negative for a suitable choice of separation. An elementary counting argument and the Iwaniec-Sarnak supremum bound then give the claimed lower bound.
item.dc:creator: Peter Zenz

item.title: On Parameterization of Some Problems in Number Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.31905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The article is devoted to the parametric solution of some Diophantine equations with two variables. In essence, we find an additional parametric relationship between the solution of the original equation and the simpler linear equation ax - by = 1. The method of hidden parameters helps to obtain a parametric representation of integer solutions for a number of problems in number theory. The method consists in that, first, instead of each quantity included in the original equation, we introduce an additional number of parameters using a linear or non-linear function, which allows us to find both connections between the parameters and some parametric solution of the desired equation. Then we reset (nullify) the introduced linear or non-linear functional dependence (hidden parameters), which in the original formulation of the problem would mean just changing the letter designation of the parameters. However, as a result of these actions, a simplified parametric solution is obtained and the found relationship between the parameters remains. In this paper, the method is discussed in detail using the example of parametric solving such Diophantine equation as the Pell equation. The method of such parameterization is also applied to problems related to Pell's equation. The methods of parameterization are discussed for the Delaunay equation, the Nagell equation and similar equations of higher powers.
item.dc:creator: S. N. Artekha

item.title: Elliptic curve rank growth in multi-quadratic extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.31925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article we give an algorithm to produce infinitely many explicit quadratic twists of a given elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ with a rational point and fixed root number. Moreover, under the Parity Conjecture (or other technical hypotheses), for each $n\geq 1$, we produce explicit multi-quadratic extensions $L_n$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, of degree $2^n$, such that the growth in rank from $\mathbb{Q}$ to $L_n$ is at least $\max\{2n+2^{n-1}-1,\,2^n-1\}$ when the root number of $E$ is $-1$, and at least $\max\{2n,\,2^{n-1}\}$ when it is $+1$. As a result, assuming Parity, we exhibit elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ and extensions of degree $2^n$ where the rank after base-extension is greater than or equal to $34$ or $30+\max\{2n+2^{n-1},\,2^n\}$.
item.dc:creator: Dylan T. Costa, \'Alvaro Lozano-Robledo

item.title: Trivial Iwasawa modules and arithmetic linking numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.31965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a computable criterion of the triviality of the unramified Iwasawa module over the maximal multiple $\mathbb Z_p$-extension of a number filed in which an odd prime number $p$ splits completely. This criterion is obtained from the description of the presentation matrix of the Galois coinvariant of the Iwasawa module by arithmetic linking numbers. The description is based on the Koch type presentation of a pro-$p$ Galois group with restricted ramification, which is analogous to the Milnor presentation of a link group from a viewpoint of arithmetic topology.
item.dc:creator: Yasushi Mizusawa, Keiji Okano

item.title: An explicit bound on $|\zeta_K(1+it)|$
item.description: arXiv:2610.32012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $n$ and discriminant $\Delta$. The estimate $|\zeta_K(1+it)|\le C_K\log{t}$, where $C_K$ is an unspecified constant depending on $K$, is a well--known result in the literature. We obtain an explicit upper bound for $|\zeta_K(1+it)|$, depending only on $n$ and $\Delta$. We also show how improvements on the bound depend on improvements on estimates of the ideal counting function $I_K$ and the residue of $\zeta_K$ at $s=1$.
item.dc:creator: Giulia Pelizzari

item.title: A Sharp Upper Bound for the Frobenius Number
item.description: arXiv:2610.32219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $0<a_1<\cdots<a_n$ be integers with $n\ge 2$ and $\gcd(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=1$. Their Frobenius number $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ is the largest integer that cannot be expressed as a nonnegative integer combination of $a_1,\ldots,a_n$. Erd\H{o}s and Graham proved the classical bound $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\le 2a_{n-1}\lfloor a_n/n\rfloor-a_n$, which depends on the two largest generators. Dixmier subsequently proved their conjecture $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\le a_n^2/(n-1)$, a bound depending only on $a_n$ and $n$ that removes the factor $2$ from the corresponding quadratic estimate. Following the Erd\H{o}s--Graham approach, we remove the factor $2$ while retaining the dependence on $a_{n-1}$, and prove $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\le a_{n-1}\lceil a_n/(n-1)\rceil-a_n-1$. This bound can be substantially smaller than Dixmier's when $a_{n-1}$ is small relative to $a_n$. For every $n\ge3$, we also construct infinitely many instances satisfying the reverse inequality, which shows that the bound is sharp.
item.dc:creator: Lin Chen, Tingwei Hu, Yuchen Mao, Guochuan Zhang

item.title: Value-distribution of Euler--Zagier type multiple zeta-functions with identical arguments on the critical line
item.description: arXiv:2610.32242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the value-distribution of the Euler--Zagier type multiple zeta-functions with identical arguments on the critical line. Mishou showed that the set of the values of the Euler--Zagier double sum with identical arguments on the critical line is dense in the complex plane under the Riemann Hypothesis. In this paper, we generalize Mishou's result to the $r$-fold Euler--Zagier multiple zeta-functions with identical arguments for $r geq 4$.
item.dc:creator: Kenta Endo

item.title: Prime Numbers of the Form $24m+1$ and Erd\"{o}s-Straus Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.32302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1948, Erd\"{o}s and Straus formulated a conjecture on Egyptian fractions. One only needs to prove the conjecture for any prime number $n$ such that $n\equiv 1\;(\mbox{mod}\;24)$. In this article, we give a necessary and sufficient polynomial condition for a number of the form $24m+1$ to be a prime number. Then we present 56 solvability polynomials consisting of our earlier tame solutions, wild solutions and the polynomials for composite numbers of the form $24m+1$. Numeric test shows that they imply the conjecture. Moreover, we give a list of 36 exponential-polynomial functions consisting of our earlier 28 tame solutions and the polynomials for composite numbers, whose numeric test shows that Howerton's conjecture on fourteen wild primes holds. Furthermore, we find a version of Goldbach conjecture modulo 24.
item.dc:creator: Yichuan Cao, Xiaoping Xu

item.title: Shintani Cocycle Decomposition of Topological Polylogarithms for Totally Real Fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.32363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compare two cohomological constructions computing special values of partial zeta functions of totally real number fields at nonpositive integers: the Shintani cocycles arising from polyhedral cone decompositions, and the Eisenstein classes obtained from the topological polylogarithm. In particular we prove that the specialization of the topological polylogarithm at a nonzero torsion point coincides in cohomology with the Shintani class up to an explicit sign and error term, and obtain Siegel and Klingen's classical rationality Theorem.
item.dc:creator: Julio de Mello Bezerra

item.title: Binary Quadratic Forms, Shintani Lifts, and Twisted L-Values
item.description: arXiv:2610.32470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F\in S_{2k}^{new}(M,\chi^2)$ be a Hecke newform, and $D$ a fundamental discriminant with $(-1)\chi(-1)D>0$. Via the Shimura Correspondence, we get associated modular forms of half-integral weight, and Waldspurger showed that for such $g=\sum c_nq^n \in S_{k+1/2}(4M',\chi;F)$, if $c_{|D|}(g)\neq 0$, then $|c_{|D|}(g)|^2 \propto |D|^{k-1/2}L(F\otimes \overline{\chi}\otimes \chi_D,k)$. Kohnen refined this in the case that $f\in S_{2k}^{new}(N)$ for $N$ odd and squarefree, making explicit $|c_{|D|}(g)|^2$ for $g \in S^+_{k+1/2}(4N;f)$. However, $c_{|D|}(g)=0$ unless $\left(\frac{D}{p}\right)=w_p(f)$ for all $p|N$. In this paper, we produce more generally $g \in S^+_{k+1/2}(4\ \mathrm{lcm}(N,N_1^2),\chi;f\otimes \chi)$, where $\chi$ is a character of odd squarefree conductor $N_1$, using a family of generalised Shimura/Shintani maps $\Psi_\chi^D,{\Psi_\chi^D}^*$ due to Kojima and Tokuno. Extending their work (and Kohnen's), we compute its Petersson norm, and give an explicit formula for all the $|c_m(g)|^2$. The key technical ingredient is an explicit set of representatives for $L^0_{M_1,M}(M_1^2D^2)/\Gamma_0(M)$ of binary quadratic forms. We also use a new multiplicity-one result based on work of Kohnen, Ueda, and Waldspurger. In the case $N_1|N$, we reconstruct forms previously considered by Baruch-Mao and Prasanna, which change Kohnen's condition to $\left(\frac{D}{p}\right)=-w_p(f)$ for all $p|N_1$, thus relating twisted $L$-values to squares of Fourier coefficients for all classes of discriminants.
item.dc:creator: Mark Chambers

item.title: The limiting zero counting measure for Eisenstein series
item.description: arXiv:2610.32590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For an arbitrary congruence group $\Gamma$, we study the zeros of a generating set of the space of Eisenstein series of varying even weight for all $\Gamma(1)$-conjugates of $\Gamma$. These zeros form a $\Gamma(1)$-invariant set that descends to the modular orbifold $Y(1)$. It is known that, as the (even) weight tends to infinity, the set of zeros converges in the Hausdorff metric to finitely many geodesic segments. In this paper, we find the weak limit of the normalised counting measure of the zeros in the (natural) orbifold sense: if a geodesic occurring in the Hausdorff limit is parametrised by the unit circle $S^1$ via a M\"obius transformation then the limit measure on this segment is the pullback of the Haar measure on $S^1$ by that transformation. For the proof, we first show a version of the Poincar\'e--Lelong theorem for orbifold curves, and then apply it on $Y(1)$ to reduce the problem to computing the scaled limit of the subharmonic functions $\log |E|$ associated to Eisenstein series $E$. This turns out to be the maximum of the negative logarithm of the modulus of finitely many linear functions supported on the relevant geodesic segments, and we finish the proof by showing that the associated measure has no atoms and making explicit, on each open segment, the distributional Laplacian of this function in terms of the argument measure. The non-atomicity allows us to conclude a sublinear growth rate in the weight for the total order of all Eisenstein series at a given point in $Y(1)$, and weak convergence also of the non-orbifold measure to the same limit.
item.dc:creator: Gunther Cornelissen, Mahya Mehrabdollahei

item.title: Hausdorff dimension of canonical height spectra
item.description: arXiv:2610.32625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Hausdorff dimension of the closure of the canonical height values associated to finite compositions of two rational maps. For rational maps with common periodic critical points, a nonzero local--global height discrepancy gives a nonempty set of starting points with positive-dimensional spectra. For polynomials, equality of the normalized logarithms of the leading coefficients at every place forces dimension zero; a single-place discrepancy gives positive dimension under boundedness at the other places. We construct rational cubic pairs with spectra of dimension \(\log2/\log3\). The spectrum dimension gives a lower bound for the growth exponent of the number of distinct orbit points of bounded height. At the degree exponent, positive Hausdorff measure gives matching growth bounds for multiplicatively dependent degrees. For independent degrees, a restriction of the covering intervals and a Diophantine rotation estimate give a lower bound with logarithmic loss of exponent strictly less than \(1/2\). Quadratic monomial examples show that the spectrum dimension can depend on the starting point even when both individual orbits are infinite.
item.dc:creator: Wayne Peng

item.title: The Hardy--Littlewood asymptotic for primes $p$ and $p+4$ from a uniform zeta-ratios conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.32672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the Hardy--Littlewood asymptotic for prime pairs of difference four from a restricted uniform two-over-two zeta-ratios formula. The formula has error $O_\varepsilon(U^{1/2+\varepsilon})$, real parts of all four shifts in $[3/64,5/64]$, and imaginary parts of absolute value at most $U^{1/4}$. For a fixed real smooth weight supported in $(1,101/100)$, we obtain an error $O_\varepsilon(x^{-1/16+\varepsilon})$ in the correlation sum with weight $W(n/x)^2/n$. Adding the Riemann hypothesis improves this error to $O_\varepsilon(x^{-3/8+\varepsilon})$. The proof retains the crossed zero residues in Mellin inversion and estimates their mixed term with the logarithmic-derivative integral. Two nonnegative time weights have the same diagonal term and opposite coefficients for the difference four. We deduce the logarithmic asymptotic for the weighted prime-pair sum $B_4$ and an asymptotic for the second finite difference of integrals of squared increments of the truncated Chebyshev function. The latter is connected to a logarithmically weighted M\"obius approximant in the Nyman--Beurling criterion by finite identities.
item.dc:creator: SeungJu Lee

item.title: A genus-two spectral curve of the Riemann $\Xi$-function: Real Structure and Certified Arithmetic Separation of Periods
item.description: arXiv:2610.32694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We associate a compact genus-two real spectral core with a transverse logarithmic-derivative discriminant of the Riemann $\Xi$-function. Directed interval arithmetic certifies its branch geometry, a real $P_{\mathrm{III}}(D_6)$ scalar-normal-form realization, and associated Kummer and Shioda--Inose models. Zero-action resonance reduces to rationality of two real period ratios. Their certified heat motion yields generic local nonresonance and Diophantine separation, while explicit Farey windows impose denominator barriers of $1{,}036{,}003$ and $140{,}769$ throughout $|\kappa|\le3\times10^{-10}$ in the heat time $\kappa$. Fixed-point irrationality and exact Picard rank remain open. The heat tangent differs from the matched fixed-exponent isomonodromic direction, but admits a local moving-exponent curve lift. Separately, a reciprocal-head canopy certificate combined with published finite-RH and rectangular time-barrier verifications bounds the de Bruijn--Newman constant by $\Lambda\le433/2500=0.1732$ without a QRH assumption. These local arithmetic and global analytic results share a phase--transverse bridge; no equivalence between core nonresonance and RH is asserted.
item.dc:creator: Michel Planat

item.title: Spectral convergence associated with Weil's quadratic form
item.description: arXiv:2610.32704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we study a distinguished self-adjoint extension of the differentiation operator on a Hilbert space defined by the Weil quadratic form localized to a finite interval. The local quadratic form is determined by data from finitely many places, without requiring the zeros of the Riemann zeta function as input. We prove that the positive eigenvalues of this extension converge to the distinct positive ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function as the interval expands. We also prove that the associated normalized spectral entire functions converge locally uniformly on the complex plane to the canonical product over these distinct ordinates. The key step is an identity expressing the inverse of the local extension as a compression of the inverse of a global self-adjoint operator.
item.dc:creator: Masatoshi Suzuki

item.title: Traces of Green's functions on $\mathbb{H}^q$ over point-hypersurface pairs
item.description: arXiv:2610.32825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The famous algebraicity conjecture of Gross and Zagier for the values at CM points of higher Green's functions was recently proven by Bruinier, Li and Yang. Motivated by this the values of the automorphic Green's function at pairs of special points in hyperbolic $3$-space $\mathbb{H}^3$ were studied by Herrero, Imamo\={g}lu, von Pippich and Schwagenscheidt, and an analogous algebraicity result for traces of Green's functions was established. In this paper, we consider higher automorphic Green's functions $G_{s}(P,Q)$ on hyperbolic $q$-space $\mathbb{H}^q$ for $q\geq 2$ when the spectral parameter $s$ is a positive even integer, and prove an explicit finite formula for their traces over geodesic hypersurfaces in one of the variables. This formula provides a geometric interpretation of the traces of Green's functions for every choice of a point in $\mathbb{H}^q$ for the second variable. As an application, we obtain rationality results when the second variable is evaluated at a special point providing further evidence that such results for traces of Green's functions do not depend on any underlying complex structure.
item.dc:creator: Claudia Alfes, Jens Funke, Sebasti\'an Herrero, \"Ozlem Imamo\={g}lu

item.title: Rational Points on Affine Varieties over Finite Fields and Polygonal Number Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.32930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Authors, in an earlier work, proved that prime power subsequences of the polygonal numbers corresponding to $4$, $6$, $8$, and $10$ arise naturally as the numbers of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points of certain double Danielewski surfaces. In this work, authors generalize the previous construction and give a new family of affine varieties over finite fields such that the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points of these varieties give the prime power subsequence of every polygonal number sequence.
item.dc:creator: Sakshi Gupta, Anit Kuckian, Indranath Sengupta

item.title: Power Sum Varieties over Finite Fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.32056v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a family of affine algebraic varieties over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ defined by systems of power sum polynomials. Our main goal is to investigate their geometric and arithmetic properties, with particular emphasis on the structure and dimension of their singular loci. Using tools from the theory of symmetric polynomials and generalized Vandermonde determinants, we establish explicit conditions under which these varieties are complete intersections and prove that, in a broad range of parameters, their singular loci have codimension at least two. As a consequence, we derive normality and irreducibility results for both the affine varieties and their projective closures. Building on this geometric analysis, we obtain estimates for the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points and deduce effective existence results for solutions of systems of symmetric power sum equations over finite fields. Finally, we apply these results to the study of Waring's problem and to the analysis of the cost of computing a $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational point of such systems.
item.dc:creator: Nardo Gim\'enez, Juan Francisco Gottig, Miguel Palacios, Mariana P\'erez, Melina Privitelli

item.title: Partial rigidity and q-additive functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32445v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A system $(X,\mu, T)$ is partially rigid with constant $\delta>0$ if there exists an incresing sequence $(n_k)$ such that $\displaystyle \liminf_{k \to \infty } \mu(A \cap T^{-n_k}A) \geq \delta \mu(A)$ for every measurable $A \subset X$. The partial rigidity rate is the largest constant of partial rigidity. We characterize the partial rigidity rate of subshifts arising from $q$-additive functions $\pmod M$ in terms of quantities arising from B\'esineau's theorem. With this, we build a family of strongly $q$-additive functions to deduce that the collection of partial rigidity rates for substitution subshifts is dense in $[0,1]$ answering a question of Donoso, Maass and the author.
item.dc:creator: Trist\'an Radi\'c

item.title: Deterministic Root-Finding over Finite Fields with Elliptic Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.32508v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Finding the roots of a polynomial over a finite field $\mathbb F_q$ in deterministic polynomial time is a long-standing open problem. Classical deterministic methods work in the multiplicative group $\mathbb F_q^\times$ and are efficient only when $q-1$ is smooth, which is rarely the case. We propose a method that replaces $\mathbb F_q^\times$ by the groups of rational points of an elliptic curve $E$ and of its quadratic twist $\widetilde E$. The computation splits into an offline phase, which depends only on $\mathbb F_q$ and outputs a short \emph{elliptic preprocessing datum} $\mathcal D$, and an online phase, which processes the input polynomial. Writing $\Xi(\mathcal D)$ for the largest prime factor of $\lvert E(\mathbb F_q)\rvert\cdot\lvert\widetilde E(\mathbb F_q)\rvert$, the online phase is deterministic and finds the roots of any $f\in\mathbb F_q[X]$ of degree $n$ within $\widetilde O(\Xi(\mathcal D)^2\,n\log^2 q+n^\omega\log q+n\log^3 q)$ operations in $\mathbb F_q$. A precursor of our method is an algorithm by R\'onyai, which recovers the roots through Galois computations over number fields, relies on GRH, and comes with a polynomial bound of unspecified degree; in contrast, our online phase works entirely over $\mathbb F_q$ and is unconditional. Moreover, $\mathcal D$ can be certified deterministically and unconditionally in time polynomial in $\log q$ and $\Xi(\mathcal D)$. We conjecture that every $\mathbb F_q$ of large enough characteristic admits a datum with $\Xi(\mathcal D)\leq(\log q)^{O(1)}$, and support this with a heuristic and with experiments. Constructing such a datum in polynomial time remains open.
item.dc:creator: Pierre-Jean Spaenlehauer

item.title: Metaplectic cusp forms and the large sieve
item.description: arXiv:2403.13151v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a power saving upper bound for the sum of Fourier coefficients $\rho_f(\cdot)$ of a fixed cubic metaplectic cusp form $f$ over primes. Our result is the cubic analogue of a celebrated 1990 Theorem of Duke and Iwaniec, and the cuspidal analogue of a Theorem due to the author and Radziwill for the bias in cubic Gauss sums. The proof has two main inputs, both of independent interest. Firstly, we prove a new large sieve estimate for a bilinear form whose kernel function is $\rho_f(\cdot)$. The proof of the bilinear estimate uses a number field version of circle method due to Browning and Vishe, Voronoi summation, and Gauss-Ramanujan sums. Secondly, we use Voronoi summation and the cubic large sieve of Heath-Brown to prove an estimate for a linear form involving $\rho_f(\cdot)$. Our linear estimate overcomes a bottleneck occurring at level of distribution $2/3$.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Dunn

item.title: Series expansions by generalized Bessel functions for functions related to the lattice point problems for the $p$-circle
item.description: arXiv:2408.02613v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The lattice point problems of the $p$-circle (for example, the astroid), which a generalized circle for positive real numbers $p$, have been solved for approximately $p$ more than 3, based on the series representation of the error term using the generalized Bessel functions by E. Kr\"{a}tzel and the results of G. Kuba. On the other hand, for the cases $0<p<2$, the method via this series representation cannot make progress. Therefore, in such cases, it is necessary to consider another method. In this paper, we prove that certain functions closely related to the problems can be displayed as series by newly generalized Bessel functions based on the property $p$-radial, generalization of spherical symmetry, and highlight the possibility that attempts to solve the problems via this display are suitable especially for the cases $0<p\leq1$. This study is based on the harmonic-analytic method by S. Kuratsubo and E. Nakai, using certain functions generalizing the error term of the circle problem by variables and series representation of the functions by the Bessel functions.
item.dc:creator: Masaya Kitajima

item.title: Hausdorff dimension of the graph of the unweighted error-sum function of continued fractions
item.description: arXiv:2507.16536v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the unweighted error-sum function $\mathcal{E}(x) \coloneqq \sum_{n \geq 0} (x - p_n(x)/q_n(x))$, where $p_n(x)/q_n(x)$ denotes the $n$th convergent of the continued fraction expansion of $x \in \mathbb{R}$, and we prove that the graph of $\mathcal{E}$ has Hausdorff dimension $1$. The key ingredient is an exact formula for the oscillation of $\mathcal{E}$ on fundamental intervals, which we obtain in a symbolic space of continued fraction sequences containing non-realizable sequences. Using the same framework, we also give a new derivation of the upper bound $3/2$ of Ridley and Petruska (2000) for the Hausdorff dimension of the graph of the relative error-sum function $P(x) \coloneqq \sum_{n \geq 0} (q_n(x)x - p_n(x))$. Moreover, we present an alternative argument based on M\"obius inversion and summation over coprime convergent denominators, and we explain why the square coverings used for $P$ cannot yield an upper bound smaller than $3/2$.
item.dc:creator: Min Woong Ahn

item.title: Geodesic clustering of zeros of Eisenstein series for congruence groups
item.description: arXiv:2509.16108v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a set of generators for the space of Eisenstein series of varying even weight $k$ for any fixed congruence group $\Gamma$ and study the set of all of their zeros taken for all $\Gamma(1)$-conjugates of $\Gamma$ in the standard fundamental domain for $\Gamma(1)$. We describe (a) an upper bound $\kappa_\Gamma + O(1/k)$ for their imaginary part; (b) a finite configuration of geodesics segments to which all zeros converge in Hausdorff distance as $k \rightarrow \infty$; (c) a finite set containing all algebraic zeros for all weights. The bound in (a) depends on the (non-)vanishing of a new generalization of Ramanujan sums. The proof of (b) originates in a method used to study phase transitions in statistical physics. The proof of (c) relies on the theory of complex multiplication. The results can be made quantitative for specific groups. For $\Gamma=\Gamma(N)$ with $4 \nmid N$, $\kappa_\Gamma=1$ and the zeros tend to the unit circle, whereas if $4 \mid N$, $\kappa_\Gamma=2$ and the limit configuration includes parts of vertical geodesics and circles of radius $2$. In both cases, for sufficiently large $k$, the only algebraic zeros are at $\mathrm{i}$ and $\exp(2\pi \mathrm{i}/3)$, and, for $4 \mid N$, at $2\mathrm{i}$. For $\Gamma(N)$ with $N$ odd, we use finer estimates to prove a trichotomy for the exact `convergence speed' of the zeros to the unit circle, as well as angular equidistribution of the zeros as $k \rightarrow + \infty$, implying weak convergence of the normalized zero counting measure on $Y(1)$ to the image of the argument measure on the lower arc of the fundamental domain.
item.dc:creator: Sebasti\'an Carrillo Santana, Gunther Cornelissen, Berend Ringeling

item.title: Density results for $r$-gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta-function
item.description: arXiv:2603.17334v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $0<\gamma_1\leq \gamma_2\leq \ldots$ denote the positive ordinates of the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta-function. A result first announced by Selberg states that there exist absolute constants $\Theta, \vartheta>0$ such that for each $r\in \mathbb{N}$, \[ \limsup_{n\to \infty}\frac{\gamma_{n+r}-\gamma_n}{2\pi r/\log \gamma_n}\geq 1+\frac{\Theta}{r^\alpha} \qquad \text{and}\qquad \liminf_{n\to \infty}\frac{\gamma_{n+r}-\gamma_n}{2\pi r/\log \gamma_n}\leq 1-\frac{\vartheta}{r^\alpha} \] where $\alpha$ may be taken as $2/3$, or as $1/2$ if one assumes the Riemann hypothesis. This was recently proved by Conrey and Turnage-Butterbaugh under RH and by Inoue unconditionally. We prove that in fact a positive proportion of $r$-gaps are large (and small) to the above extent, and we provide explicit estimates for the sizes and proportions of these gaps. In the case $r=1$, this quantitatively improves an unconditional result of Simoni\v{c}, Trudgian and Turnage-Butterbaugh.
item.dc:creator: Tianyu Zhao

item.title: On Sun's Conjectures for Truncated Jacobi-Symbol Determinants via Supersingular Elliptic Curves
item.description: arXiv:2608.08509v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the truncated Jacobi-symbol determinants $$\{c,d\}_n=\det\!\left[\left(\frac{j^2+cjk+dk^2}{n}\right)\right]_{2\le j,k\le n-2}$$ proposed by Zhi-Wei Sun in \cite{ZWSun} and prove Conjectures 5.1(i), 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 5.5, 5.6(i), 5.7, 5.8, a case of 5.6(ii) of \cite{ZWSun}, Conjecture 4.8(i) of \cite{Sun2019} and some strengthened forms. All results follow from a single unified approach: for a prime $p$, we diagonalize the nonzero-residue matrix indexed by $\mathbb{F}_p^\times$ and reduce the vanishing of determinants to the supersingular reduction of certain CM elliptic curves. The same framework extends naturally to further families of parameters, suggesting a general mechanism behind identities of this type.
item.dc:creator: Guo Li, Xiaojun Yan

item.title: Optimising Selberg's method for critical zeros
item.description: arXiv:2609.15329v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We revisit Zhuravlev's 1974 quantitative form of Selberg's sign-change method for the zeros of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line. Zhuravlev's work, originally in Russian and little known in the West, established an explicit positive proportion of such zeros. Using modern techniques we optimise the arithmetic mean value at the heart of the method and obtain the strongest result yet known from Selberg's method, proving that more than $6.78\%$ of the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie on the critical line.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Pearce-Crump

item.title: Averages of Artin characters and their relation to the Davenport--Heilbronn theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.01837v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We bound the error term in the counting function of cubic extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$ by $\mathcal{O}_\epsilon(X^{\theta+\epsilon})$, with $\theta < 2/3$, improving upon results due to Bhargava, Taniguchi, and Thorne. The proof proceeds by relating a certain discriminant-reducing sieve, due to Bhargava, Shankar, and Tsimerman, to averages of Artin characters associated with the Artin $L$-function $\zeta_K(s)/\zeta(s)$, with $K$ a cubic field. Conditional on the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) for Dedekind zeta functions $\zeta_K(s)$, we obtain further savings and show that the error term is $\mathcal{O}(X^{2/3-1/51+\epsilon})$. Moreover, for the analogous smooth counting problem, we obtain a bound $\mathcal{O}(X^{1/2+\epsilon})$ for the error term, conditionally improving results of Shankar, S\"odergren, and Templier. Our arguments can also handle finitely many splitting conditions. The methods we use to study cubic fields are natural extensions of methods which are used to study the one-level density associated with the above family of Artin $L$-functions. In this direction, we improve the admissible support $[-\sigma,\sigma]$, from the previously known admissible value $\sigma < 2/5$, to $\sigma < 1$, conditional on the GRH. This also proves that at least $75\%$ of these $L$-functions are non-vanishing at the central point, conditionally improving upon results of Shankar, S\"odergren and Templier. Finally, one may study similar questions over a rational function field $\mathbb{F}_q(T)$, with $q$ coprime to $2$ and $3$. Here, we obtain a proportion of non-vanishing of at least $75\%$ for the analogous family of $L$-functions. Furthermore, we obtain a bound $\mathcal{O}\left(X^{1/2+\epsilon}\right)$ for the error term in the counting function of cubic function fields, improving previous results of the author. Over function fields, our results are unconditional.
item.dc:creator: Victor Ahlquist

item.title: Explicit second moments of symplectic Siegel transforms
item.description: arXiv:2610.03499v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give two alternate formulations for the second moment formula of the Siegel transform over $\mathrm{Sp}(2n, \mathbb Z) \backslash \mathrm{Sp}(2n,\mathbb R)$, previously established by Athreya-Konstantoulas and Kelmer-Yu. We also provide several applications that demonstrate their usefulness.
item.dc:creator: Kristian Holm, Seungki Kim

item.title: Galois Groups of Trinomials with Small Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.22764v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We calculate the Galois group of $f = x^n + ax^k + b \in \mathbb{Z}\left[ x \right]$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ for all $1 \leq \left| ab \right| \leq 3$, $n$ sufficiently large and $k$ coprime to $n$. In particular, we prove that the Galois group of $f$ is the maximal one that its factorization type allows. We give a criterion for the Galois group of a factor of a trinomial to be symmetric, with an eye towards future applications. To the best of our knowledge, the only previously known explicit example of polynomials of degree $n$ with bounded coefficients and Galois group $S_n$ is $x^n - x - 1$, while recent results show that the probability that a random polynomial of degree $n$ with reasonably bounded coefficients has Galois group $S_n$ tends to $1$ as $n$ tends to infinity. Using our calculation, one can construct many new such explicit examples.
item.dc:creator: Hilel Garmi

item.title: Stevens' Approach to Kloosterman Sums on Split Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.24399v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a uniform framework for Stevens' approach to Kloosterman sums on split groups over $p$-adic fields. The main result reduces the bounding of Kloosterman sums to that for the so-called Pl\"ucker-constrained sets, which are certain subsets of affine spaces constrained by conditions giving by the Pl\"ucker coordinates. We then give a nontrivial bound for the Kloosterman sums on the exceptional group $G_2$. As an application, we obtain the regularity of Bessel distributions associated with generic representations on $G_2$.
item.dc:creator: Li Cai, Haoran Liu, Mingyu Yang, Wenyan Yang

item.title: Small and large gaps between zeros of Dirichlet $L$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.28527v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every fixed primitive Dirichlet $L$-function and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove unconditionally that infinitely many consecutive zeros have spacing less than $1/2+\varepsilon$ times the mean. Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, we also prove a positive proportion of such spacings for the Riemann zeta-function, and infinitely many spacings greater than $3.63$ times the mean for every fixed primitive Dirichlet $L$-function.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Durkan, Andrew Pearce-Crump

item.title: Distinction of the Steinberg representation with respect to a symmetric pair
item.description: arXiv:2410.03247v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a non-archimedean local field of residual characteristic $p\neq 2$. Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over $K$, let $\theta$ be an involution of $G$ over $K$, and let $H$ be the connected component of $\theta$-fixed subgroup of $G$ over $K$. By realizing the Steinberg representation of $G$ as the $G$-space of complex smooth harmonic cochains following the idea of Broussous--Court\`es, we study its space of distinction by $H$ as a finite dimensional complex vector space. We give an upper bound of the dimension, and under certain conditions, we show that the upper bound is sharp by explicitly constructing a basis using the technique of Poincar\'e series. Finally, we apply our general theory to the case where $G$ is a general linear group and $H$ a special orthogonal subgroup, which leads to a complete classification result.
item.dc:creator: Chuijia Wang, Jiandi Zou

item.title: Testing Transformer Learnability on the Arithmetic Sequence of Rooted Trees
item.description: arXiv:2512.01870v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study whether a transformer network can learn the deterministic sequence of trees generated by the iterated prime factorization of the natural numbers. Each integer is mapped into a rooted planar tree and the resulting sequence $\mathbb{N}\mathscr{T}$ defines an arithmetic text with measurable statistical structure. A transformer network (the GPT-2 architecture) is trained from scratch on the first $10^{11}$ elements and evaluated on next-token prediction and masked-token prediction tasks, with a Hidden Markov Model as baseline and a scaling analysis over context window, dataset size, vocabulary size and model size. The model reaches a word accuracy of about $0.4$, well above the baseline, and its performance remains stable on test blocks located at $10^{13}$-$10^{15}$, far beyond the training interval. Moreover, the likelihood assigned by the trained model separates the arithmetic text from two controls: synthetic token sequences that preserve the marginal token frequencies but not their order, with a separation that widens with the context, and sequences containing more than three consecutive square-free integers, a configuration that arithmetic forbids. These results indicate that the transformer captures regularities of the arithmetic text that go beyond its frequency profile.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Breccia, Federica Gerace, Marco Lippi, Gabriele Sicuro, Pierluigi Contucci

item.title: Khintchine dichotomy for images of self-similar measures and almost random walks
item.description: arXiv:2610.13099v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Following the celebrated breakthrough in B\'enard-He-Zhang, we prove Khintchine dichotomy for push-forwards of self-similar measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ under uniform $C^{1+\alpha}$ maps. For this, we also study almost random walks on $\mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb{Z})$ and prove their effective equidistribution.
item.dc:creator: Liyang Shao
